newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka says needs more rain to fill reservoirs.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka says needs more rain to fill reservoirs.

text.p: Southwest monsoon rains are expected to continue over Sri Lanka's hydro-catchment zones, but more water will be needed to top-up the island's power-generating reservoirs, an official of the meteorological department said.
"This year's monsoon commenced on June 10 but only became active on June 23," Jayatilleka Banda, Deputy Director of the Meteorology Department told Reuters on Tuesday.
"It is continuing and will probably continue through the month of August," he said.

Over the past three weeks, the Castlereigh and Laxapana hydro-catchment zones in southcentral Newara Eliya district recorded up to 70mm of rainfall on certain days, but these had been sporadic and offset by 1-3 day dryspells, Banda said.
"In both areas we have recorded fair amounts of rain," he added. "These falls are not bad, but not enough to raise water levels of tanks to top level."
Rainfall in hydro-catchment zones is crucial to Sri Lanka's electricity needs as the country is dependent hydro-power.
As a result of a dry monsoon sweeping across the southwest from May to Oct 1996, reservoir levels dipped to record lows forcing the government to impose eight-hour per day power cuts.

Dry weather has hit the country's tea production this year. After last year's record harvest of 258.4 million kg, output this year is expected to be closer to 250 million, mainly due to lack of rain, industry analysts say.
